summary: Redis is installed and persistent on node1. The generated inventory credential is root-only, authentication is enforced, and service/data recovery succeeded after a full node restart.
actions_performed: Enabled AOF persistence with every-second fsync under /var/lib/redis.
Created the inventory ACL identity and disabled unauthenticated default access.
Generated the credential on node1 and stored it in /etc/redis-inventory.env with mode 0600 and root:root ownership.
Bound Redis to node1's managed IP and persistently allowed TCP/6379 through firewalld.
Verified data persistence across Redis service restarts and a full node restart.

evidence.summary: Redis is active and enabled; AOF is enabled and healthy, and the proof value survived service restarts.

evidence.requirement: Dedicated inventory identity and root-only generated credential
evidence.summary: The credential was generated on-node without disclosure. The environment file is root:root mode 0600; authenticated WHOAMI returns inventory, while the default user is disabled.
Redis listens on node1's managed IP, and TCP/6379 is allowed in both runtime and permanent firewall configuration.

Evidence captures the healthy pre-restart boot identity and data, safe reboot acknowledgement, changed boot identity, active/enabled Redis, authenticated inventory access, retained proof value, healthy AOF state, protected credential file, and restored firewall configuration.
